newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares continue to fall, end bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares continue to fall, end bourse lower.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of 30 blue-chips ended bourse trade over one percent lower on Thursday as a slightly lower dollar and overnight losses on Wall Street hit sentiment on the floor of the Frankfurt bourse.

The DAX index extended a fall begun in late trade on Wednesday to end the day down 37.72 points, or 1.17 percent, at 3,196.03 points. Declines had set in late the previous day after a wave of selling on U.S. markets.

A weak performance on Wall Street weighed on the market and jitters ahead of Friday's triple witching options expiry added to volatility, but dealers said the feeling on the market was that prices had been pushed up to unrealistic levels.
"We haven't had really negative numbers but I suppose people are thinking now that it can't get better than this. And we really need to clear the air here," said a Frankfurt dealer.

A larger than expected rise in German January M3 money supply data on Thursday briefly added to pressure on the market, although the effect was shortlived as economists said this would not motivate a German interest rate hike.

Insurer Allianz AG Holding was hit in early trade, but pared earlier losses to end down 13 marks at 3,227 points. The insurer was hit by profit-taking after announcing a double digit rise in earnings for 1996, in line with expectations.
Engineering group Mannesmann AG ended down 5.50 marks at 672.50. Earlier it announced a doubling of its telecommunications earnings and said it planned to raise its dividend by one mark.
Although some dealers said the dividend hike was less than had been expected, Mannesmann's overall message was neutral to positive.
Siemens AG ended bourse down 1.35 marks at 84.45 marks, despite a projection that its semi-conductors division would triple sales by the year 2001.
Dealers said the market was pessimistic on the division in general, whose profits fell to 603 million marks in the 1995/1996 business year from 793 million.
Volkswagen AG was the only winner in bourse trade, ending up 3.50 marks at 801.50 marks, lifted by news that a Spanish truckers strike, which had hit its production there, was over.
